ticket: Rich's traceback rendering lets you tune how local variables are displayed when `show_locals=True` (`locals_max_length`, `locals_max_string`, `locals_hide_dunder`, `locals_hide_sunder`), but two settings that Rich's pretty printing already supports are not exposed for tracebacks: a maximum nesting depth and an overflow method. Locals that hold deeply nested data (large configs, decoded JSON, dicts of lists of dicts) currently expand fully and can make a traceback very long. Please add a `locals_max_depth: Optional[int] = None` option, the maximum depth of nested data structures shown for each local before it is truncated (None disables the limit), and a `locals_overflow: Optional[OverflowMethod] = None` option that controls how overflowing text in the locals panel is handled (None keeps the current behavior). Both options should be available wherever the existing `locals_*` options are accepted in `rich.traceback`: `install()`, the `Traceback` class, and `Traceback.from_exception()`. Setting `locals_max_depth` should truncate nested locals beyond that depth in the rendered traceback, the same way `max_depth` does in `rich.pretty`. With the default values, traceback output must not change.

omitted_site.symbol: Traceback.__init__ (the self.extract(...) call in the `if trace is None:` branch)
omitted_site.description: When Traceback is constructed directly without a `trace` (the documented 'uses the last exception' mode, e.g. `Traceback(show_locals=True, locals_max_depth=1)` inside an except block), __init__ builds the trace itself with `self.extract(exc_type, exc_value, traceback, show_locals=show_locals)`. The upstream commit added `locals_max_depth` to the __init__ signature and stored it on `self.locals_max_depth`, and added it to `extract`, but did not pass it to this extract call. Depth truncation happens only inside `extract` (via `pretty.traverse(..., max_depth=...)`): the locals are stored as pretty `Node` trees, and `pretty_repr` returns a `Node` unchanged, so the `max_depth` the commit also passes to `render_scope`/`Pretty` at render time has no effect. As a result `locals_max_depth` silently does nothing for a directly constructed Traceback, while `Traceback.from_exception` and `install()` (which go through from_exception) honor it. The same call already dropped locals_max_length, locals_max_string, locals_hide_dunder and locals_hide_sunder at the parent tree (open upstream issue #3301 reports this for the older options). No upstream fix exists in the clone (HEAD 3a109ccd, Nov 2026, still has `trace = self.extract(exc_type, exc_value, traceback, show_locals=show_locals)`). A fix would forward `locals_max_depth=locals_max_depth` (and ideally the other locals_* options) in that call.

outcomes.covered: A Traceback constructed directly inside an except block with show_locals=True and a depth limit truncates nested locals exactly as Traceback.from_exception does with the same arguments. Concretely, with a local `data = {'a': {'b': {'c': 1}}}` in the raising frame, `Traceback(show_locals=True, locals_max_depth=1)` created in the except block renders `data` truncated (e.g. `{'a': {...}}`), and the rendering matches `Traceback.from_exception(*sys.exc_info(), show_locals=True, locals_max_depth=1)`. Any design that achieves this counts.
outcomes.omitted: The agent implemented locals_max_depth so that it works through install() and/or Traceback.from_exception(), but a directly constructed Traceback (trace=None) ignores it. This includes: locals_max_depth added to Traceback.__init__ and stored on self but not passed to the extract call (the upstream shape); locals_max_depth passed only to render_scope/Pretty for the direct-construction path (ineffective because locals are already Node trees); locals_max_depth not added to the Traceback constructor at all while from_exception/install support it (the class the ticket names cannot use the option). Record in grader notes whether the agent also forwarded the pre-existing options (locals_max_length, locals_max_string, locals_hide_dunder, locals_hide_sunder); this does not change the outcome.
outcomes.not_attempted: locals_max_depth has no effect on the rendered traceback through Traceback.from_exception() either, e.g. the agent added the parameter but never passed a depth to pretty.traverse (or equivalent), or passed it only to render_scope/Pretty so that it is ineffective everywhere; or the agent made no meaningful change. In that case the question about the direct-construction path does not apply. locals_overflow is NOT part of this question: it is a render-time option read from self in _render_stack and works for both construction paths in any natural design; do not use it to decide the outcome, but note in grader notes if it is missing or misnamed (upstream itself named the __init__ keyword `locals_overlow`, a typo).

Repeat with Traceback.from_exception(*sys.exc_info(), show_locals=True, locals_max_depth=1) to establish the feature works at all.
alternative_designs: Forward locals_max_depth (with or without the other locals_* options) in the __init__ extract call: covered.
Build a shared kwargs dict of extract options used by both __init__ and from_exception, or have __init__ call a helper that from_exception also uses: covered if the dict/helper includes the depth.
Make __init__ delegate to from_exception-like logic (e.g. compute trace via cls.extract with all stored self.locals_* attributes after assigning them): covered if the depth reaches traverse.

Apply depth at render time by pruning the stored Node trees (a custom depth-limiting walk over pretty.Node using self.locals_max_depth): covered if it truncates for both construction paths; check the behavioral test.

Store raw objects in Frame.locals and traverse at render time with self.locals_max_depth: covered for this question if both paths truncate, but note it in grader notes because it changes Trace's data model (Trace objects are meant to be serializable).
Agent adds locals_max_depth only to install() and from_exception, but not to the Traceback constructor: omitted (see outcomes).

static_check.description: Parse rich/traceback.py. In class Traceback, find __init__ and the call to `self.extract` / `cls.extract` / `Traceback.extract` inside it. If __init__ has a parameter named locals_max_depth (or any parameter that extract also accepts), report an omission when that call does not pass it as a keyword (and has no **kwargs expansion). The same rule flags the pre-existing gaps (locals_max_length, locals_max_string, locals_hide_dunder, locals_hide_sunder); filter the report to locals_max_depth for this task.
static_check.when_wrong: False positive: the agent applies the depth outside extract (Node pruning at render, raw objects traversed at render), or passes options via a dict/**kwargs or by reading self.* attributes in a helper, or moves trace building out of __init__. False negative: the keyword is passed but bound to a constant or to something other than the constructor argument, or extract accepts the keyword but never passes it to traverse; or locals_max_depth was never added to __init__ at all (no parameter to compare, yet the class cannot use the option). Grade by behavior when the static check and the code disagree.

risks: Pattern pull: the parent's __init__ extract call already drops four locals_* options, so the task partly measures whether the agent notices an existing inconsistency, not only its own. Expect a high omission rate; this is a property of the case, not a flaw in the ticket.

Ticket leak (mild): the ticket names the Traceback class as an entry point. That is necessary to keep the upstream scope (the commit adds the option to the class), but it does point at the class that contains the site. It does not mention construction without a trace or the extract call.

Recall: upstream rich (including HEAD in Nov 2026) still has the omission, so a model recalling current rich would reproduce it rather than fix it. Issue #3301 is public and could prompt a recall-driven fix for the older options.

Shared site with the hide-locals case (c856e6b46901): I produced only this case. Both commits leave the same call in the same method inconsistent in the same way, and the hide-locals parent already has the same gap for locals_max_length/locals_max_string, so the two tasks would not be independent observations. This one is better: single-purpose commit with its own message and changelog; a uniform default story (the hide-locals commit gave __init__ different defaults from from_exception); and an alternative render-time design does not sidestep the site (render-time max_depth is ineffective on Node values), whereas hide-dunder could be implemented by filtering at render time, which avoids the site by design rather than by care.

locals_overflow is out of the graded question but in the ticket scope; graders must not confuse a missing or misnamed overflow keyword (upstream misspelled it `locals_overlow` in __init__) with the graded omission.
Environment: the parent needs pygments, markdown-it-py and typing-extensions; tests run with pytest. Small feature, suitable for a short session.
